notes: ACCESS: plain direct fetch, no proxy needed (matches the prior Home-Decor pass). Salesforce Commerce Cloud storefront (Sites-bassett-Site). robots.txt carries no anthropic-ai / ClaudeBot / Claude-Web directive. TREE: built from two independent sources and reconciled. (1) The rendered mega-menu in the homepage HTML (div.custom-dropdown-menu), whose custom-dropdown-link-header divs give the site's own section names: SEATING / RECLINING / LEATHER / TABLES & CABINETS under Living, plus DINING FURNITURE, BEDROOM FURNITURE, OFFICE FURNITURE and OUTDOOR FURNITURE. (2) sitemap_index.xml -> sitemap_0.xml (2650 locs, 262 non-PDP). The sitemap exposed about 25 real subcategories the mega-menu never shows, e.g. /living/sectionals/l-shaped-sectionals, /living/recliner-chairs/power-recliners, /bedroom/beds/headboards, /dining/chairs-and-benches/*, /office/bookcases-and-etageres and /living/fabric-seating/*. All 193 department URLs were fetched and their h1, breadcrumb, PLP element id and count header recorded; parent/child relationships were taken from the on-page breadcrumb (e.g. 'Home > Living > Recliner Chairs'), not from URL shape. QTY: source of truth is the rendered listing header .result-count.text-b2-global ('N Results'). Every leaf was then re-fetched a second time at ?start=0&sz=400 and its unique data-pid tiles inside div.product-grid counted. Header and enumeration agreed EXACTLY on 64 of 69 leaves, and no count drift appeared between the two reads. Four leaves (Reclining Sectionals, Extendable Dining Tables, Dining Chairs with Casters, Platform Beds) render no result-count element at all, so their qty comes from enumeration; the method was first calibrated on three pages that DO have a header (162 / 106 / 4) where it matched exactly, and each of these four returns the identical tile set at default paging as at sz=400, so each is a single complete page. The one mismatch, Leather Loveseats, is explained on its row: the header (40, stable over four reads) is correct and the sz>=100 grid over-fetches to 72 from the sibling leather-sofas category. HIERARCHY (rule applied: a node with extractable children becomes a grouping row and only the children carry qty). Grouping rows were emitted for Sectionals (93), Chairs (173), Ottomans & Benches (72), Recliner Chairs (62), Reclining Furniture (128), Fabric Seating (284), Leather (146), Coffee & Cocktail Tables (38), Credenzas & Media Consoles (29), Dining Tables (35), Chairs & Benches (51), Beds (106) and Dressers & Chests (33). Those parent totals are given here for reference only and are deliberately written to no row. DUPLICATE PLPs COLLAPSED (same PLP element id, same h1, same count served at several URLs): /bedroom/accent-chairs and /office/accent-chairs are both plp-living-accent-chairs (58) and are kept once as Living Room > Chairs > Accent Chairs; /office/loveseats is plp-loveseats (75), kept once under Living Room. DEAD SLUG: /dining/dining-tables/round-dining-tables silently serves the PARENT listing (h1 'Dining Room Tables', breadcrumb 'Home > Dining', plp-dining-tables, 35) instead of 404ing, so it was dropped rather than recorded as an 11th dining row. OVERLAPPING AXES: Bassett merchandises the same upholstery under a product-type tree, a material tree (Fabric Seating / Leather) and a motion tree. The material tree is kept because both branches are genuine SFCC category nodes with breadcrumbs and distinct exact counts, and its two grouping rows are flagged so nobody sums them with the product-type rows. The motion roll-ups /living/motion (137) and /living/motion/motion-chairs (117) were DROPPED as a pure synonym duplicate of the RECLINING section that the mega-menu does not show; /living/occasional-and-accent-tables (101), /outdoor/dining (17) and /outdoor/living (48) were dropped for the same reason, being unlabelled roll-ups of categories already recorded individually. EXCLUDED per scope: all Rugs (including /bedroom/rugs, /office/rugs, /dining/performance-rugs and /outdoor/outdoor-rugs), all Lighting (the /home-decor lamp and pendant categories and their /bedroom, /dining and /office /lighting clones), the whole Bedding tree, Accent Pillows, Pillow Inserts, Throws, Mirrors, Wall Decor, Cutting Boards, and Cabinet Hardware / Knobs & Pulls. Mattresses & Bases (/bedroom/mattresses-and-bases) is excluded as bedding; Bassett splits it cleanly from Beds, so no flag was needed there. EXCLUDED per the navigation-junk rule: every Shop All, In Stock Ready to Ship, New in <dept>, Best Sellers, Sale, Clearance and Order Swatches page; the entire Designer's Choice / Collections layer (Bedroom Collections, Dining Room Collections, Sofa & Sectional Collections, Occasional Table Collections, Outdoor Collections and their roughly 30 named collection children such as Andora, Copenhagen, Newbury, BenchMade, European Farmhouse, Carolina, Stockten, Beckham, HideAway, HomeWork, Z4 Sleepers, Bonavista, Susanna and Oasis); /living/club-level-reclining-furniture (60) as a Bassett sub-brand listing page; /living/build-your-own-sectional (26) as a configurator landing page; /bedroom/custom-upholstered-beds (76, a Designer's Choice duplicate of Upholstered Beds at the same 76); /living/modern-accent-chairs (13, which serves clp-living-room-furniture); and the /shop-by-style/* pages. NAMING: sub_category uses the site's own node names. The seven Outdoor leaves are prefixed 'Outdoor' (four of the seven already carry it in their own h1) to keep them distinct from the identically named indoor categories in a flat sheet. Department grouping rows use the department h1 wording: Living Room, Dining Room, Bedroom, Home Office, Outdoor.
